genericRisk:
The token work and the "no icons, words only" decision genuinely do not read as a vibe-coded webapp, and I will defend that. What still does:

(1) The shell is Settings.app. Bottom dock with three cells (§9.15), tab row (§9.6), content in bottom sheets that slide up over the thing you came to look at (§5.3), segmented controls everywhere (§9.3). That is the default phone chassis of 2020-2026. It is not wrong, but nothing in it was earned from painting — swap the words and it is a banking app.

(2) `--c-corporate: #2f3a40` (§7.1) is slate blue-grey, the stock "professional neutral" of every dashboard ever shipped. In an app whose whole subject is that Markus owns 54 specific pigments, the one interactive ink being a generic grey is a missed opportunity and it reads as a template default. Pick an ink that comes from the material — a Payne's grey or an indigo that actually exists in the box, named as such in a comment — and the page stops looking like a theme.

(3The software tells: `--ff-fixed` and a whole type role for hex codes (§8.3, §9.7), "Match: excellent" as a graded badge with its own third colour token, `AI HELP` carrying an eyebrow heading as a peer of `THE PLAN` (§9.9), the `--z-*` / `--speed` token block. A painter never reads `#6e5e47`.

(4) `--radius-medium: 0.8rem` on every button, input and segmented control plus `--radius: 1.2rem` on every sheet and card (§7.4) is rounded-everything by another route. A plan sheet is set with hairlines and alignment, not with corners. The list (§9.8) is specified as rounded cards with `--radius-medium`; it should read as a legend — rows, rules, tabular numbers — which is what the printed sheet looks like and what the painter already knows how to read.
keep: Decision 8, no icons (§1.8). Every control carries a word. With gloves on and in a hurry, a word is unambiguous and an icon is a guess. It also kills the 22 px cross, the 28 px chevron and the two floating buttons over the picture in one stroke, which is the cheapest real improvement in the document.

Abolishing the pointer tooltip and the floating panel (§1.4, §1.5, §13 on `floating.js` and `RecipeTip.vue`). Both were useless with a brush in hand. The card slot with three possible contents at one priority (§2.2) is the right structural answer.

The touch model written as values with a named enforcement file (§6) and repeated as checks (§14.3). 48 px minimum, 56 px primary, 8 px apart, 32 px slider thumb with `Less`/`More` steppers and a readable value (§9.10) — that is a slider I can actually set to 12 with a wet glove.

The copy. `1:3 with water, like tea.` / `Then let it dry completely.` / `Back to the photo as it is` / `Pick the colour of a medium wash on white paper, not the colour straight from the pan or tube.` (§9.7, §9.9, §9.13) is written by someone who has mixed paint. Keep every word of it.

The contrast table (§7.2) is real, not decoration. I checked `--c-copy-light` #655e55 on `--c-background` #f2efe8 by hand: 5.56:1, the spec claims 5.6:1. A specification whose numbers survive being checked is worth building from.

Mix and layer as one interface, rule by rule (§4), and promoting the layer chips into the view bar at every breakpoint instead of keeping `LayerStrip.vue` as a narrow-screen special case. Two parallel universes was the worst thing about the old build.
mustFix: §15.5 admits the phone is not decided: whether the colour list is a sheet or a third of the screen "wants the owner's hands on the prototype". That is the one question the brief's phone section asked, and the specification defers it. Decide it here, and decide it against the sheet: §3.1 step 4 has the list open at 72 % of the screen (picture reduced to a 28 % strip) and then *close on every selection*. Reading through 20 colours is 20 open-and-close cycles, and while I am choosing I cannot see where that colour sits in the picture — which is the entire question. Make the phone list a fixed lower third under the picture, as on iPad portrait (§5.4), scrolling in place, with the card replacing the list content rather than covering the picture.

§5.3's arithmetic is wrong and the central promise of §1.1 ("the picture is always on screen") does not survive it. The table gives masthead 56 + readout 40 + view bar 48+8+48 = 104 + dock 64, i.e. 264 not the stated 96-for-the-view-bar figure, and it ignores `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` (34 px on the phone it was measured on) and the fact that `100dvh` in Safari is about 745 px, not 844. Real picture height: ~447 px, ~391 px in layer mode, ~327 px once the close-up strip exists — and then the card sheet's 184 px peek sits on top of it, leaving about 140 px of picture. Redo the budget against 745 px and state the minimum picture height the design guarantees; if it is under about 300 px, chrome has to go (start with the view bar's second row, as §15.1 suspects).

The recipe — the only sentence that puts paint on paper — is specified to be truncated in both places it appears. §9.8: `list__meta` is "one line, ellipsis". §5.3 and §9.4: `stage__readout` is one fixed line, `white-space: nowrap`, `overflow: hidden`. The example string in §9.4, `Colour 7 · 12 % of image · 2 x 663 Sepia brown + 1 x 485 Indigo`, is about 430 px at `--fs-small`; the phone is 390 px wide minus padding. It will read `…2 x 663 Sepia bro…`. Give the readout two lines on the phone (reserve both, so nothing shifts), put the recipe on its own line in the list row, and let it wrap to two — never ellipsis on a paint name or a number.

Nowhere does the specification say that choosing a colour from the list shows me where it is in the picture. §4 promises isolation only for "tap an area" in the picture; §9.8 gives the selected row a background and opens the card and stops there. The code already isolates the selected mix (`PaintingCanvas.vue`, the `shown()` guard and the blanking at line 244) — so this is a specification omission, not a redesign, and it is the one that matters most: "where is number 7 on my paper" is the question I ask forty times a session. State it in §9.8: selecting a row isolates that mix in the picture exactly as tapping an area does, and the picture must be visible while the list is open (see the phone item above).

§9.8 makes every wash and coat segment a 48 px button and never says what pressing one does. The current build selects that single wash (`PaletteList.vue` line 147, `analysis.selectEntry`) and marks it active (line 62); the spec drops both the action and the active state. A painter pressing `M` expects the picture to show only the medium wash — that is "one wash at a time" made visible, and it is the most useful thing on the row. Specify the action and the selected state, or make the segments non-interactive; an unexplained 48 px button is worse than a label.

On the iPad there is no way to get the picture alone. §5.4 fixes the rail at `clamp(28rem, 38dvh, 40rem)` permanently — 280-400 px of an 1112 px screen gone at all times — and §1.8 removed folding (`PanelToggle.vue` deleted, "`collapsed` stops being read", §13). `Full size` (§9.5) is a zoom, not a layout state. While I am actually painting, for twenty minutes at a stretch, I want the plan at full screen and every control out of the way. Add one state, not a control cluster: a `Picture only` toggle in the view bar that hides the rail (or the dock) and leaves the readout; one tap back.

`New photo` is the first row of a list of 48 px full-width rows, 8 px apart, one tap from the masthead (§1.7, §3.1 step 7, §11), and it throws away the analysis including every colour I overruled by hand. The specification writes an in-place confirmation for `Delete box` and for deleting a saved picture (§9.13, §9.20) and none for this, nor for `Next sample`. That breaks the brief's own rule about dangerous things being far from constant ones. Put `New photo` and `Next sample` at the *bottom* of the Picture sheet, separated by `--m-vert`, with the in-place confirm you already use elsewhere — and say in the confirmation what is lost ("3 colours you changed by hand").

§9.10: "the steppers fire `@change` on each press". Moving Colours from 20 to 12 is eight presses, and the spec has just queued eight full re-analyses on a tablet while the painter watches `Analysing…` flicker. Specify it properly: the stepper changes the displayed value immediately and the analysis fires once, about 400 ms after the last press (or on blur). Same for the slider drag.

§9.7 gives `Change colour` as a word with no surface behind it. This is the one place where I overrule the maths because I know the mix better than the computer does, and the specification does not say what opens, what I see while deciding, or how I compare the result against the photo; §12's `forms.css` inventory ("field, slider, stepper, check, input, select") has no colour control at all. Specify it: what control, where it appears (in the card, not a new sheet), that the picture updates live, and that `Reset to photo` is adjacent — and make it reachable without a native picker's fine drag.

§9.7's two swatches, `Target` and `Your mix`, are `--size-swatch` 40 px, stacked, each with its own 1 px inset border and a row gap. That is the single colour judgement this whole app exists to support, and it is specified in the hardest possible form to judge: two small patches separated by a border and a strip of paper. Make the pair one block of two abutting fields, no border and no gap between them, at least 72 px tall across the card's full width, with the labels outside. Edge-to-edge is how an eye compares two colours; everything else is guesswork.

§2.2's card priority makes the spot card unreachable during the step walk (step card always wins), while §9.4's readout table also shows only the step line, and §3.1 step 3 says tapping the picture dismisses the card. So during the walk — the one time I am actually painting — tapping the picture either does nothing or closes my step. Resolve it in §2.2: during the walk, tapping a spot keeps the step card and puts the spot's layers in the readout (or in a second line of the step card), and the picture never dismisses the walk.

§9.1 has no modifier-aware hover or active state, so pressing an already-selected control inverts it. Selected is "background `--c-corporate`, text `--c-white`"; active and hover are both "background `--c-accent`" (pale) with `--c-corporate` text. Press the active view option and it flashes from near-black to near-white. Worse, the layer chips (§9.5) carry the layer's own paint colour as their background — the one thing a chip is for — and `:active` replaces it with `--c-accent`. Specify `--active:hover` and `--active:active` separately, and give the chips a press state that does not touch their fill (an inset ring).
shouldFix: Nothing on screen remembers what I have already painted. The mix list numbers by area share, largest first (`analysis.js` line 864), which is not painting order, and §4 denies mix mode a step walk, so in mix mode the specification offers no order at all and no state between "selected" and "not selected" (§9.8). A session is three hours with twenty-minute drying gaps; when I come back I need to see which mixes are down. Add one row state (`list__item--done`) and a 48 px `Painted` toggle in the card. No logic in `src/lib/` changes.

The screen goes to sleep during the walk and I unlock it with a wet glove. The specification does not mention it once. A wake lock while the step walk is open, released on close, with a line in the step bar saying the screen is being kept awake.

`Colours are an estimate from one swatch: test the wash on a scrap first.` appears only as a row in §10's table of replaced `title` attributes. That is the most important honest sentence in the product and it is homeless. Put it in §9.7's colour card under the recipe, and on the printed sheet.

Print gets one paragraph (§5.7) and is specified as "unchanged in substance", but paper is what stands on the table while a wash dries — the iPad is asleep. In particular the step card's `Mix` / `Paint` / `Then` lines and the dilution ratios are not specified to appear on the layer sheet. Say what the printed sheet carries, per mode.

`Clear` sits in the paint box action row next to `Auto` and `Update mixes` (§9.13), with 8 px between them, and `Revert` is "mix only" — so in layer mode one gloved thumb wipes the base paints with no way back. Give `Clear` the in-place confirm, or give layer mode a `Revert` too.

`AI HELP` as the fourth section of the Plan tab with its own eyebrow heading (§9.9) gives it the same weight as `THE PLAN`. It is already in the `More` sheet (§11). Demote it to a single quiet row at the foot of the tab.

Two sheets can be open at once — the card at peek plus `Plan` at 72 % — and all sheets share one `--z-sheet: 30` (§7.4) with no stacking or mutual-exclusion rule stated (§5.3, §9.12). Say which sheets close which.

§1.8 says the only drawn graphics are the picture, the swatches, the recipe bars and the favicon; §9.11 then specifies a drawn SVG tick path inside the checkbox. Minor, but the house rules are the pass/fail criterion, so reconcile the sentence.

§7.3 steps the type at 768 px and calls it "the only deviation", but the brief's real complaint was that the phone base never steps *down*. It does not step down here either — `--fs-copy` is 16 px at 320 px wide as it is at 767. At 320-360 px, with a three-paint recipe and a `20 colours in 14 mixes` count line, state a step down for `--fs-small` and `--fs-mini` or the wrapping comes back.
verdict: This is the most disciplined of the specifications I have been shown and I would still not paint from it yet. The structural calls are right — the picture never scrolls away, the tooltip and the floating panel are gone, words instead of icons, one interface for both methods, a touch model written as numbers that someone can be held to. The copy is written by someone who has mixed paint, and the contrast figures survive being checked by hand. But the phone, which is what I complained about, is the weakest part of the document: §15.5 openly leaves the main phone decision to the prototype, §5.3's height budget is arithmetically wrong by about 100 px and ignores the safe area and Safari's real viewport, and the answer it does give — the colour list as a sheet over 72 % of the screen that closes on every pick — is worse than the scroll it replaces, because it hides the picture at exactly the moment I am asking where a colour sits in it. Three things that matter more than any layout are missing or truncated: the recipe is specified with `ellipsis` in both places it appears, so paint names get cut; nothing says that picking a colour from the list shows me where it is in the picture, although the code already does it; and the Target-versus-mix comparison, the one judgement the app exists for, is two 40 px patches with a border and a gap between them, which is the hardest way to compare two colours. Add to that no painted/not-painted state anywhere, no way to get the picture alone on the iPad, `New photo` as the first row of a tap-list with no confirmation, and a stepper that fires a re-analysis per press, and this is a plan I would test on cheap paper first. Fix the twelve items below — they are all inside this design, not a different one — and it becomes a tool I would keep on the table.

A serious, unusually complete specification that gets the structure right and then fails the arithmetic on the one screen it was told to fix. The IA decisions in §1 are defensible and §10/§13 are better work than most teams produce. But §5.3's phone height budget is computed against a viewport the phone does not have, §9.13 specifies a paint box that cannot fit its own contents in its own stated height, §9.1's interaction colours differ from their surfaces by ~1.15:1 so tap feedback is invisible in dark mode, and the three features that a free browser account cannot use (Save, Print, Frame) are listed in §11 as working everywhere with no locked state specified anywhere. It is buildable in outline and guessy in exactly the places where the previous build failed. Round 2 should not redesign; it should re-measure.
mustFix: §5.3, the phone height budget, is computed against a viewport that does not exist. The table reserves "56 + 40 + 96 + 8 + 64 = 264 px" and concludes "about 560 px for the picture" at 390 x 844. Two errors. First the sum is wrong: §5.3 itself specifies the viewbar as 4.8 + 0.8 + 4.8 rem = 104 px, not 96, so the chrome is 272. Second, and fatally: the shell is `height: 100dvh; overflow: hidden`, so the page never scrolls, so Safari never minimises its toolbars. On an iPhone 14 the usable viewport is roughly 690-740 CSS px, not 844 - and the evidence screenshot `docs/ui/evidence/phone-settings-2026-10-12.png` is an in-app browser with a top bar AND a bottom toolbar, which is worse again. Real picture height: about 700 - 272 = 428 px. In layer mode, minus the 56 px chip row of §5.3's own note: 372 px. With the `note` bar up: 324. With the consent banner of §9.18 on first visit (title + paragraph + two 56 px buttons, about 180 px, and §9.18 places it above the dock): roughly 190-250 px of picture on the first screen the owner will ever see. Recompute every budget in §5.3 and §5.4 against the small viewport, state the measured figure per device, and either drop the viewbar to one row on the phone or move `Outlines`/`Numbers` into the card.

§5.3 + §9.3 reproduce the exact failure in the evidence screenshot, one level smaller. The screenshot fails because a fixed multi-column grid was given words that do not fit. `viewbar__toggles` is specified as `grid-auto-flow: column; grid-auto-columns: 1fr` with four cells (`Outlines`, `Numbers`, `Full size`, `Frame`); at 390 px with the 1.6 rem gutters that is 83 px per cell, and `Full size` at `--fs-copy` 16px/600 wraps. At 320 px it is 66 px per cell and `Outlines` alone is wider. Worse, §9.3 gives every segmented option `min-width: 7.2rem`: the phone view switch has four options, 4 x 72 = 288 px plus internal rules, against 288 px of available width at 320 px - it overflows its own container, while §14 check 2 asserts "no two labels collide at any width from 320 px upward". The `--fs-small` drop at <= 374 px does not change `min-width`, so it fixes nothing. Specify: the toggle row wraps to two rows of two below 375 px, or the toggles collapse to a single `View options` row; and make the segmented `min-width` a floor that yields (`min-width: min(7.2rem, 100%)` or a stated per-breakpoint value).

§9.13 specifies a paint chip that cannot hold its own contents. `chip--paint` is "5.6 rem tall" (56 px) with `min-width: 15rem`, containing a 4.0 rem swatch plus, in the text column: the number and name (`--fs-small`, two lines maximum = ~38 px), the `Pan`/`Tube` word at `--fs-mini` under the name (~14 px), the brand line, and the meta word `in use` - per §10's row for `PaintChip`, a second line reading `Schmincke Horadam . Sepiabraun . colour estimated`. That is four to five lines of text in a 56 px box, and at 390 px the grid gives two columns of 171 px, leaving 123 px of text width for a 48-character line. Either raise the chip height and state it, or state explicitly which of those strings is dropped on the phone. This is the single densest surface in the app (54 paints) and it is the one the spec measured least.

§9.13's paint box action row is the seven-buttons-wrapping-into-ragged-rows problem that §1.7 fixed for the `Picture` sheet and forgot here. The head carries `Auto`, `Revert`, `Clear`, `Update mixes` (primary, 5.6 rem), `Close` - five buttons, all >= 48 px tall, >= 8 px apart, on one line, in a sheet 358 px wide on the phone. `Update mixes` alone needs ~120 px. No wrapping rule, stacking rule or per-breakpoint behaviour is given. Specify the phone arrangement explicitly: `Close` in the sheet head per §9.12, `Update mixes` as a full-width sticky footer button, and `Auto` / `Revert` / `Clear` as a secondary row or inside the `Selected paints` group head.

The three features a free browser account cannot use are specified as if they always work. `stores/collection.js:41` gates saving behind `pro.require`, `ControlsPanel.vue:302` gates print, and `stores/analysis.js:306` gates the close-up frame unconditionally (`require(false, ...)`). For the default browser user with accounts on, `Save to collection`, `Print / PDF` and the `Frame` toggle all open the purchase sheet instead of doing the thing. §11 lists all three as "yes" on every device; §9.5's `Frame` toggle gets an `aria-pressed` state it will never enter; §9.4's readout table has rows for "framing on, no frame yet" but none for "this needs the full version"; §9.20 says only "Pro: copy unchanged". Specify the locked state: how a gated control is marked before it is tapped (a word, not a colour, and not `disabled` - it must stay tappable to reach the offer), what the readout says, and how the purchase sheet returns the user to the action they were attempting (`pro.reason` already carries it).

§9.1's interaction colours are invisible. Hover, `:active` and the selected list row all resolve to `--c-accent`. In dark mode `--c-accent` #2f2b27 against `--c-white` #232120 is 1.15:1; against `--c-background` #191816, 1.66:1. In light, `--c-accent` #e6e1d4 against `--c-white` is 1.30:1 and against `--c-background` 1.13:1. The `:active` text change to `--c-corporate` does not rescue it in dark, where `--c-corporate` #cfd8dc and `--c-copy` #ece7dc differ by about 1.2:1. So the brief's "tap feedback must be immediate and visible" is satisfied by a change no one can see, on the device the brief names as primary, in the mode the brief says is used in the evening. §7.2's contrast paragraph only measures text tokens and never says so. Give `:active` a cue that survives: the selected-state inversion (`--c-corporate` fill) held for the press, or a 2 px inset `--c-corporate` ring. And separate hover from selected - as written, hovering an unselected list row on an iPad trackpad makes it look selected.

Non-text contrast is never addressed, and the design depends on 1 px borders everywhere. `--c-border` is 1.43:1 against `--c-white` in light and 1.30:1 in dark. It carries: the segmented control's outer border and internal rules (§9.3), `button--quiet`'s entire affordance (§9.2), the rail division (§5.5), the note bar, inputs, and the unchecked checkbox box in §9.11 ("2 px `--c-border`"). In dark mode an unchecked checkbox and an unselected quiet button are effectively borderless. WCAG 1.4.11 wants 3:1 for control boundaries, and studio glare wants more. Add a second token for control boundaries (not a second `--c-border` meaning) at >= 3:1 against both surfaces, and state which uses take it.

§9.7 lists `Change colour` as a line in the colour card and never says what it opens. Today it is `<input type="color">` (`EntryEditor.vue`), whose iOS/iPadOS picker is a hue square requiring pixel precision - the exact thing §6 bans and §6's own drag table does not list. Specify the affordance: a sheet of coarse swatches plus hue/saturation/lightness on the `.slider` block of §9.10 (which already has `Less`/`More` steppers), or state that the native picker is accepted and why it clears the glove test.

§5.4 specifies a `rail__card` on iPad portrait that its own numbers make unreachable, and §2.2 says so. The rail panel is `clamp(28rem, 38dvh, 40rem)` = 280-400 px; `rail__card` is "max-height: 50 % of the panel" = 140-200 px, with a stated minimum of 24 rem = 240 px, "if it cannot have 24 rem, it opens as `sheet--card` instead". 200 < 240 always, so the card is always a sheet on iPad portrait and the whole `rail__card` paragraph in §5.4 is dead text that an implementer will nonetheless build. Delete it, or change the clamp so the branch can be taken, and move the one real rule (the 24 rem fallback) to the one place §5.4 says it lives, `rail.css`.
shouldFix: §5.3 and §3.1 step 5 break the app's core loop on the phone. The `Plan` sheet opens at 72dvh; on a ~700 px viewport that leaves about 140 px of picture under the masthead, and §5.3 says the scrim "covers only the area the sheet does not" - i.e. it covers the picture - and then claims in the same sentence "the picture stays legible behind it". Both cannot be true. Moving `Colours` from 20 to 12 and watching what happens is the reason this app exists. Specify a reduced height for `sheet--plan` (a peek that leaves the picture unscrimmed, raised only on demand), or no scrim for the plan sheet, and say which.

§9.4's own example line does not fit the phone it is written for. `Colour 7 . 12 % of image . 2 x 663 Sepia brown + 1 x 485 Indigo` is about 62 characters; at `--fs-small` (14 px) that is roughly 420 px against 358 px of available width, with `white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden`. It truncates inside the recipe - the only part that matters - while keeping `12 % of image`. Reorder the line (recipe first, share last) or allow two lines on the phone and raise the reserved height from 4.0 rem accordingly.

§5.2 contradicts itself on safe areas: "applied once, on `.app`, plus `padding-bottom` on `.dock` and on every sheet". `.app` already consumes `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` as padding, so the dock gets a second 34 px of dead space on an iPhone and sits 34 px above the home indicator. Also, `.app { height: 100dvh; padding: env(...) }` needs `box-sizing: border-box` to not overflow, and the spec never states the reset's box-sizing. Pick one owner of the bottom inset - the dock, since it is the painted surface - and state the box model.

The spec removes a working capability without declaring it. §4 and §9.5 say that while the step walk runs, "the view bar's switch *is* the step view switch". Today `LayerSteps.vue` carries its own switch alongside the main one, so a painter mid-step can still flip to `Photo` or `Sketch`. After this change they must close the walk to look at the photo. §11 hides this behind one row reading "View switch | view bar | yes". Either keep both (a second row in the viewbar during the walk) or state the loss and justify it.

§9.14 loses a reachable action. `CloseupStrip.vue` has a per-thumbnail remove today; §9.14 deletes it and puts `Remove` in the close-up bar, which §9.14 itself says only appears "while a close-up is open". So a close-up can no longer be removed from the base picture - it must first be opened. Say so, or put `Remove` in the strip's active thumbnail state.

§9.3 ("never more than four options") contradicts §9.13 ("a `segmented` of box names"). Paint boxes are unlimited and user-named (`stores/paints.js:136`, `maxlength="40"`). Six boxes called "Horadam travel set" in a `flex: 1 1 0` segmented with `min-width: 7.2rem` is the collision in the evidence screenshot, verbatim. Boxes need a different control - a select, or a list in the sheet body.

Screen-reader behaviour is almost entirely unspecified, which the brief asks for by name. §9.8 defines the list visually but gives no accessible name for a row, no announcement for a wash or coat segment button (what does the `L` segment say?), no list semantics. The readout of §9.4 is the replacement for the removed tooltip and the carrier of every status including `Analysing...`, yet no live region is specified - and if it is made live, the fine-pointer hover variant will fire on every mouse move. §9.12 moves focus into a sheet and back but never says the sheet traps focus, is `aria-modal`, or makes the rest `inert`. Specify: row names, segment names, one polite live region for the readout that updates only on selection and status (not hover), and the dialog semantics.

§9.12 and §9.13 contradict each other on committing changes. The sheet closes on Escape, on a scrim tap, and on `Close`; the paint box "keeps today's rule that closing applies pending changes". So Escape silently commits a paint selection and re-analyses - and `Update mixes`, specified as the primary button in §9.13, then does nothing that closing does not. State which one commits, and what the other is for.

§5.2's rule "where a region would be shorter it is given `min-height: 24rem` and the region above it gives way" is not implementable as written. In a `grid-template-rows` shell with `minmax(0,1fr)` on the stage, "gives way" has to be a concrete rule. Say it: the stage is the only flexible row, and name the floor below which a sheet opens at peek height instead.

§6 claims every drag has a non-drag path, but close-up framing only half-has one. The tap path places a frame "at 40 % of the picture"; the two 4.8 rem corner handles are the only way to change its size, and that is a drag. Add `Smaller` / `Bigger` steppers next to `Use this part` and `Cancel` in the framing toggle row - and note that row then has four cells at 83 px on a phone (see the viewbar finding).

§9.2 styles `Delete account` as `button--plain`: `--c-copy-light`, underlined, no border - identical to `Close`, `Hide`, `Manual` and `Privacy`. A destructive, irreversible action rendered as the quietest thing in the system, in the same `More` sheet as the legal links. `button--danger` exists; use it for the entry point, not only the confirmation.

No initial state is specified. §3.1 step 1 asserts "the sample picture is already analysed and fills the middle of the screen", but `App.vue` calls `analysis.loadSample(true)` on mount and the worker runs for a moment. What the stage shows before the first result - and what it shows when `analysis.error` is set from `Could not load image: ...` (`stores/analysis.js:297`) and there is no canvas at all - is nowhere in §9.4's readout table or §9.4's stage rules. §9.4 says the readout is "never empty"; specify its first-run and no-picture strings, and what occupies the picture area in both cases.

Text scaling is never tested against a shell that cannot scroll. Every chrome row is a fixed `rem` height (masthead 5.6, viewbar 10.4, readout 4.0, dock 6.4) inside `height: 100dvh; overflow: hidden`. A user at 24 px default text size gets ~400 px of chrome on a 700 px viewport and a clipped picture with no scroll fallback, and §14 checks width from 320 px but never text size. Add an acceptance check at 200 % text, and a rule for what collapses first.

§9.5 never says what a soloed layer chip looks like. It gets `aria-pressed`, but §9.1's selected state is "background `--c-corporate`" - which would paint over the one thing the chip exists to show, the layer's colour. Specify the solo cue on a coloured chip (a 2 px `--c-corporate` ring at `outline-offset` plus a non-colour mark), since this is the only level-1 control whose meaning is carried by colour.

Declared-but-unused tokens invite a second system: `--c-corporate-hover` appears in §7.1/§7.2 and is never referenced in §9 (every hover is `--c-accent`); `--shadow-flat`, `--gap-3x` and `--m-vert-2x` likewise have no consumer. Either assign them or drop them - §7.4's stated purpose is "so no implementer invents a second naming scheme".

§8.1's `font-display: swap` on a same-origin variable font, with no `size-adjust`/`ascent-override` fallback metrics and no `preload`, will reflow a layout whose rows are fixed-height and whose labels are already at the edge of fitting (see the viewbar finding). `optional` plus a metrics-matched fallback is the right call for a fixed grid; state it.
keep: §10 is the best section in the document and should survive round 2 untouched in method: every `title` that carries meaning, named, with a specific new home. That is the brief's hardest requirement and the only part of this spec that is fully checkable against the code. It is right.

§9.4's readout: one permanently reserved line that never shifts the layout, with a coarse-pointer and fine-pointer string written out for every state. Replacing a pointer-following tooltip with a fixed line is the correct mechanism, and writing both strings per state instead of saying "adapt for touch" is what makes it buildable.

§4's rule table. Forcing mix and layer through one row grammar, one card slot and one tab position, and then promoting `LayerStrip` from a narrow-screen fallback to the viewbar at every breakpoint on the argument that "which layer am I looking at" is the same question as "what does the picture show" - that is a real IA argument, not a tidying exercise, and it answers the brief's "two universes sharing a font".

§13's migration table, which states per file what changes and, more usefully, what does not: `SCALE`, `drawMixes`, `drawLayers`, `drawSketch`, `regionAtCanvasPixel` untouched; the arrow-key handler kept; the apply-on-close rule kept; no store API renamed. A presentation-layer rework that names its own blast radius is rare.

Killing `floating.js`, `RecipeTip.vue` and the `@dblclick` resets with named replacements rather than leaving them as "to be revisited", and §9.10's `Less`/`More` steppers labelled in words with `aria-label` naming the control - the exact-value path the brief demanded, without a symbol.

Writing the hint copy out in §9.9 rather than leaving placeholders, including the layer-mode variants and the `Auto`/by-hand split for `Layers`, which matches the real condition in `ControlsPanel.vue`.

§8.2's font argument is made on legibility grounds with stated reasons (`1` with a foot serif, `7` without a bar, true `tnum`, x/cap ratio) and rejects Inter primarily on metrics rather than on taste. That is what the brief asked for and most teams would have written a paragraph about character.
genericRisk: "The token set and the prose are not generic - warm unbleached paper, one interactive ink, no icons - but the rendering of it is. Three things will make it read as another default webapp. First, `--c-corporate` #2f3a40 is the only interactive colour and §9.1 spends it as a solid fill with white text at `--radius-medium` on every selected state: the active tab, every segmented option, the dock cells, the layer chips, and 20+ selected paint chips in the box. A grid of 54 chips with 20 of them filled slate-at-8px-radius is the slate-700 pill vocabulary of every admin template, and it also swamps the paint swatch inside the chip - the one thing on that screen that is supposed to be the saturated element. Second, §7.4 defines one `--shadow` (0 0.2rem 2.4rem rgba(...,0.18)) and §5.3/§5.5 apply it to the sheet, the card, the rail panel and implicitly the dock: that is the stock bottom-sheet look the brief's \"no drop-shadow-on-everything\" is aimed at, and the design does not need it - it already has `--c-border` and a `--c-shade` scrim to separate layers. Third, §9.9's plan is four uppercase letter-spaced eyebrows over stacked label/value/slider rows, and §9.15's dock is three equal cells; together they are the settings page and tab bar of every SaaS app of the last five years. Underneath all of that: the preamble claims \"the software is the plan sheet around it\", and that claim produces no rule anywhere in §5 or §9. Nothing in the specification is specifically about watercolour - not the paper, not the swatch as an organising unit, not the washes, not the printed sheet the app actually produces. The position is asserted in §0 and then never spent. Round 2 should either cash the plan-sheet idea into at least one structural decision (the list as a ruled sheet, the swatch as the row's anchor rather than a 40 px square beside a number) or drop the claim and defend the design as the quiet instrument panel it currently is."
